Completeness argument (flip-closure + Wagner connectivity + K4 base, A000109 as corroboration only) is valid. Backtracker soundness spot-checked: permuted T9_0 correctly found isomorphic, doubled n=8 row pair T8_6/T8_7 correctly found non-isomorphic. Gauss-Bonnet sums re-derived independently (sum deg=6n-12 => sum defects=12). Bobenko beta calibration re-computed: flat diamond beta=pi/3, regular-tet hinge beta=2pi/3 to machine precision, matching Lemma A. Lemma B (all tetrahedra W=0) follows from Bobenko Prop 2.2 (3-point stars cospherical) and is correctly scoped; stored T4_0 W=0. Willmore extremal honestly scoped to deterministic protocol P0 as benchmark (T9_0 W=9.853014361, runner-up T9_2 9.193695508, margin 0.659), replay-certified, with explicit disclaimer that no realization-independent maximum is claimed. Proof vs computation correctly separated.

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison, not timestamp: Bobenko 0707.1318 gives Mobius-invariant discrete Willmore definition/convergence with no small-vertex census or extremal; Knoeppel et al 2311.02241 gives rolling-spheres interpretation of the same functional with no exhaustive table; Lutz math/0506520 establishes small-vertex enumeration as natural scope (vertex-transitive to n<=15) with no defect/Willmore data; OEIS A000109 tabulates only counts 1,1,2,5,14,50 (total 73) with no per-type defect multisets or distinct-count data (1,1,2,5,13,33); plantri generates combinatorial types with no curvature/energy data. Combined per-type equilateral defect-multiset table with Gauss-Bonnet certificate and distinct-multiset collision facts (e.g. doubled (0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3) at n=8; 33 distinct at n=9) is not recorded nor mechanically implied by degree data alone in those sources, and Bobenko Willmore values require realization geometry beyond combinatorics (Lemma A). No prior source covers or implies the headline exact census.

value.rationale: Headline judged separately from protocol-relative Willmore benchmark: the 73-type equilateral defect census (counts 1,1,2,5,14,50, rows summing to 12, distinct multisets 1,1,2,5,13,33, defects determine type for n<=7 but not n>=8) is a rigorously established exact invariant of a natural object (closed triangulated 2-spheres, closed initial segment n<=9). Object and invariant were motivated before computation by Bobenko/Pinkall discrete-curvature/Willmore program and Lutz small-vertex program; value not known or mechanically implied; future researcher benchmarking curvature solvers or testing discrete uniformization/energy gaps can reasonably need the precise anchor. It is not a textbook restatement (completeness + collision structure is non-trivial), not a parameter substitution, and not an unexplained number (interpreted via Gauss-Bonnet and type-vs-defect determinacy). Certification strengthens but does not substitute for this substantive distributional claim. P0-relative Willmore argmax is retained only as honestly-scoped benchmark, not the value basis.
